title: Quantum Fisher Information In A Strange Metal
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper measures quantum Fisher information in a strange metal, revealing high multipartite entanglement as the strange metal state forms.
motivation: Strange metals are poorly understood quantum states; quantifying their entanglement can provide insight into their nature.
method: The authors perform neutron scattering experiments on a strange metal and compute the quantum Fisher information from the measured dynamical spin susceptibility.
result: Quantum Fisher information increases significantly as the strange metal phase emerges, indicating the presence of genuine multipartite entanglement.
conclusion: The strange metal state is highly entangled, suggesting that entanglement is a key feature of this quantum phase.

title: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling In Time Via Autonomous Quantum Error Correction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg scaling in time for parameter estimation, overcoming the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Quantum metrology typically suffers from decoherence, limiting precision to the standard quantum limit. The authors aim to achieve Heisenberg scaling in time by using error correction to protect the probe state.
method: They propose an autonomous quantum error correction scheme that continuously corrects errors without active feedback, using a dissipative process to stabilize the probe state against noise.
result: The scheme achieves Heisenberg scaling in time for frequency estimation, with precision scaling as 1/T, where T is the total interrogation time, even in the presence of Markovian noise.
conclusion: Autonomous quantum error correction provides a practical route to surpass the standard quantum limit in noisy environments, with implications for quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Three-outcome Multipartite Bell Inequalities: Applications To Dimension Witnessing And Spin-nematic Squeezing In Many-body Systems
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: Derives three-outcome multipartite Bell inequalities and applies them to dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
motivation: To develop Bell inequalities beyond the standard two-outcome case for better detection of nonlocality and entanglement in multipartite systems, and to connect them to experimentally relevant observables like spin-nematic squeezing.
method: Constructs Bell inequalities using three-outcome measurements based on spin-1 observables, and analyzes their violation in terms of dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
result: The inequalities provide tighter bounds for dimension witnessing and can detect spin-nematic squeezing, offering a new tool for characterizing quantum correlations in many-body systems.
conclusion: Three-outcome Bell inequalities are a powerful resource for quantum information tasks in multipartite systems, with direct experimental relevance.

title: High-quality And Field Resilient Microwave Resonators On Ge Quantum Well Heterostructures
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-quality, field-resilient microwave resonators fabricated on germanium quantum well heterostructures, a key component for hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Ge quantum wells are a promising platform for hole spin qubits, but integrating high-performance microwave resonators is challenging due to material constraints and magnetic field sensitivity.
method: The authors design and fabricate superconducting microwave resonators on Ge/SiGe heterostructures, characterizing their internal quality factors and resilience to in-plane magnetic fields.
result: They achieve internal quality factors exceeding 10^5 at single-photon powers and demonstrate field resilience up to 1 T, with minimal degradation.
conclusion: These resonators are suitable for coupling to Ge hole spin qubits, enabling circuit QED experiments and advancing hybrid quantum systems with Ge-based qubits.

title: Demonstrating Optical Control Of Complex Phases In A Trapped-ion Qubit
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical control of complex phases in a trapped-ion qubit, enabling precise phase manipulation for quantum information processing.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but full control over qubit phases is essential for high-fidelity gates and complex algorithms. Optical control offers a pathway to faster and more coherent operations.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion qubit and apply optical fields to induce and control geometric phases, leveraging the ion's internal and motional states. They characterize the phase evolution via Ramsey interferometry and state tomography.
result: They achieve high-fidelity phase control with low error rates, demonstrating the ability to implement arbitrary single-qubit phase gates and showing robustness against certain noise sources.
conclusion: Optical control of complex phases in trapped ions is a viable technique for enhancing quantum gate performance, with potential applications in quantum simulation and error correction.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of A Two-voter Quantum Anonymous Voting Prototype With Continuous Variables
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a two-voter quantum anonymous voting protocol using continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Anonymous voting is a key multi-party cryptographic task; quantum protocols can provide information-theoretic security. This work aims to realize such a protocol experimentally.
method: The authors implement a two-voter quantum anonymous voting scheme using continuous-variable quantum states (likely coherent states) and homodyne detection, demonstrating the core steps of ballot casting and tallying.
result: The experiment successfully demonstrates the feasibility of quantum anonymous voting with continuous variables, achieving verifiable anonymity and correctness for two voters.
conclusion: This proof-of-principle experiment shows that continuous-variable quantum systems can support multi-party quantum communication protocols like anonymous voting, paving the way for scalable quantum network applications.

title: Entanglement As A Fairness Mechanism In Randomized Quantum Games
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes using entanglement as a fairness mechanism in randomized quantum games, showing that entanglement can ensure fair outcomes in competitive settings.
motivation: Classical randomized games often suffer from unfairness due to limited randomness or adversarial behavior; quantum resources like entanglement may provide a solution.
method: The authors design a quantum game where players share entangled states and perform local measurements, analyzing the resulting payoff distributions and fairness criteria.
result: Entanglement enables a fairer distribution of payoffs compared to classical strategies, with the degree of fairness tunable by the amount of entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement can serve as a practical resource for enforcing fairness in quantum games, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: An Almost-linear Time Decoding Algorithm For Quantum Ldpc Codes Under Circuit-level Noise
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 June 2026;

method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm that achieves almost-linear time complexity by leveraging the structure of quantum LDPC codes and using a belief propagation-like approach adapted for circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm demonstrates high decoding accuracy and near-linear runtime, making it practical for large-scale quantum error correction.
conclusion: This work advances the practicality of quantum LDPC codes by providing an efficient decoder, bringing fault-tolerant quantum computing closer to realization.
